_meta.title: Lumina — LLM Wiki for your desktop
_meta.description: Lumina — your personal LLM wiki vault for your team: Obsidian-style Markdown on disk, multiturn chat on your LLM endpoint. Version and share the vault with Box, SharePoint, or Git.

themeAriaLight: Light background on. Activate to use a dark background.
themeAriaDark: Dark background on. Activate to use a light background.
heroLeadHtml: Your personal LLM wiki vault for the team: Markdown, graph, search, and chat in one place. Keep files in Box, SharePoint, or Git for sharing and version history.

heroB2: Chat and inline assist across the same vault

heroB4: Share and version with Box, SharePoint, or Git

editorLine4Html: Lumina search feels instant — try ⌘⇧F or Ctrl+Shift+F.
expTitle: Built for the way you already work
expIntro: The layout mirrors the real desktop shell: icon rail, article list, content toolbar, and the same light palette as the product (amber primary on soft gray rails). Point the app at a vault that lives in a Box folder, a SharePoint-synced library, or a Git checkout — your team’s Markdown stays where IT already governs versions and access.
sh1Body: The article browser splits the same way as Lumina: file list on the left, toolbar with back/forward and edit controls on top, and the reading surface below — Markdown, wikilinks, and tags exactly like your Obsidian vault on disk.
sh2Title: Chat that stays beside your notes
sh2Body: The chat column uses the same centered message column as the app: user bubbles on the right with the purple tint from Lumina’s message list, assistant text on the left, and the rounded vault-colored input docked at the bottom.
sh3BodyHtml: The quick-search overlay (⌘⇧F / Ctrl+Shift+F) is centered with a soft rail-colored shell, icon plus query row, keyboard hints in the footer, and a highlighted row — matching what you see in Lumina today.
sh4Body: Nodes, soft edges, and labels echo the canvas graph: neutral disks that warm to amber when active, thin link strokes, and typography sized like the live D3 view.

featTitle: Everything you need. Nothing you don’t.
f1p: Open your existing folders — frontmatter, wikilinks, embeds, and tags travel with you. Host that folder in Box, sync it from SharePoint, or track it in Git; Lumina is just the editor over the files on disk.
f2t: Box, SharePoint, or Git for teams
f2p: There is no separate Lumina cloud for your wiki. Use Box or SharePoint for shared folders and enterprise controls, or Git for branches, diffs, and code-style review — then everyone opens the same vault in Lumina.
f3p: Summarize, expand, or refine any selection without leaving the editor flow.
f4p: Switch projects instantly; each vault keeps its own history, theme, and chat sessions.
f5p: PDF and HTML live beside your notes — research stays inside one window.
f6p: Amber accents and paper textures in both themes, plus respect for system appearance.
f7p: Wire OpenTelemetry to your own Phoenix server when you want traces — off by default.
privacyP1: No forced cloud sync. No hidden analytics pipeline. Your API keys stay in the OS keychain, your Markdown stays on disk, and Lumina only phones home to the LLM endpoint you trust — because you typed the URL yourself.
privacyP2: If you collaborate, keep the vault in Box, SharePoint, or Git — Lumina does not host a parallel wiki cloud; it reads and writes the folder those tools already version for your team.
devFootnoteHtml: End users: use the Box download above. Developers: first launch picks a vault folder; add your model under Settings. Full docs in the README.
macInstallNoteHtml:
macOS (private beta). The distributed app is not Apple-notarized yet. After installing Lumina.app to /Applications, run once in Terminal:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Lumina.app

Then open Lumina from Finder.
